'''Sir John Theodore Houghton''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|size=100%|CBE|FRS|FLSW}} (30 December 1931 – 15 April 2020) was a Welsh [[atmospheric physics|atmospheric physicist]] who was the co-chair of the [[Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change]]'s (IPCC) scientific assessment working group which shared the [[Nobel Peace Prize]] in 2007 with [[Al Gore]].<ref name="BBCobit"/> He was lead editor of the first three IPCC reports. He was professor in [[atmospheric physics]] at the [[University of Oxford]], former Director General at the [[Met Office]] and founder of the [[Hadley Centre]].<ref name="WaPo"/>

He was the president of the [[John Ray]] Initiative, an organisation "connecting Environment, Science and Christianity",<ref>"[http://www.jri.org.uk/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=112&Itemid=83 DSc for JRI Chairman]" at The John Ray Initiative website</ref> where he has compared the stewardship of the Earth, to the [[stewardship]] of the Garden of Eden by Adam and Eve.<ref>"[http://www.jri.org.uk/brief/christianchallenge.htm The Christian Challenge of Caring for the Earth] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061107115302/http://www.jri.org.uk/brief/christianchallenge.htm |date=7 November 2006 }}" at The John Ray Initiative website</ref> He was a founding member of the [[International Society for Science and Religion]]. He became the president of the [[Victoria Institute]] in 2005.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Houghton |first1=John |title=The Challenge of Sustainability. Victoria Institute Presidential Address. 1st October 2005. |url=https://www.biblicalstudies.org.uk/pdf/ft/ns/39.pdf |publisher=Faith and thought |access-date=21 April 2020}}</ref>

==Biography==
Born in [[Dyserth]], John Theodore Houghton was the second of the three sons of Sidney and Miriam (née Yarwood) Houghton.<ref name = ODNB>{{cite ODNB|title = Houghton, Sir John Theodore (1931–2020), atmospheric physicist and climate scientist|last1 = Rodgers|first1 = Clive|last2 = White|first2 = Robert S.|date = 2024|doi = 10.1093/odnb/9780198614128.013.90000381639}}</ref> His older brother, David (died 2015), became a meteorologist.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://rmets.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/pdf/10.1002/wea.2566|doi = 10.1002/wea.2566|title = Obituary: David Houghton|journal = Weather|year = 2015|volume = 70|issue = 12|page = 345|bibcode = 2015Wthr...70..345.|url-access = subscription}}</ref> The third and youngest brother, Paul Houghton, became a lecturer in engineering and was treasurer and company chairman of the John Ray Initiative, connecting the environment, science and Christianity.

The family moved to [[Rhyl]] when John was two, and he attended [[Rhyl High School|Rhyl Grammar School]] where he discovered his interest in science. He continued his education at [[Jesus College, Oxford]], gaining a BA in 1951, MA (Oxon) and DPhil in 1955.<ref name=wcc/><ref name="japanprize.jp">{{Cite web|accessdate=24 January 2023|url=https://www.japanprize.jp/en/prize_prof_2006_houghton.html|title=The Japan Prize Foundation|website=japanprize.jp}}</ref>

He was brought up as an evangelical Christian by devout Christian parents and believed in science and Christianity as strengthening each other, as well as [[Christianity and environmentalism]].<ref name = ODNB/> Houghton's evangelical Christianity combined with his scientific background made him a significant voice in evangelical Christian circles. He was a supporter of and advisor to the international Christian relief and development agency [[Tearfund]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.churchtimes.co.uk/articles/2020/8-may/gazette/obituaries/obituary-sir-john-houghton |title=Obituary: Sir John Houghton |first=Andy |last=Atkins |newspaper=[[Church Times]] |date=8 May 2020}}</ref> He was also an elder at [[Aberdyfi#presbyterian|Aberdovey Presbyterian Church.]]

In 1962, Houghton married Dr Margaret Broughton, daughter of a mill owner in Colwyn, Lancashire, and they had two children and seven grandchildren. Following her death from cancer in 1986, he set up the Margaret Houghton Memorial Fund, a research unit on medical nursing in her memory. He married his second wife, Sheila Thompson, in 1988.<ref name="WaPo"/><ref name = ODNB/>

Posts include:
* a Member of the UK Government Panel on Sustainable Development (1994–2000)<ref name="archiveis">{{cite web|url=http://www.lib.uci.edu/online/fellows/houghton.html|archive-url=https://archive.today/20030225130933/http://www.lib.uci.edu/online/fellows/houghton.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=25 February 2003|title=Chancellor's Distinguished Fellows:Sir John T. Houghton|publisher=UC Irvine Libraries|access-date=21 April 2020}}</ref>
* Chairman, [[Royal Commission on Environmental Pollution]] (1992–98)<ref name="archiveis"/>
* Chairman or co-chairman, Scientific Assessment Working Group, [[Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change]] (1988–2002)<ref name="WaPo"/>
* Director General (later Chief Executive), UK [[Meteorological Office]] (1983–91)<ref name="WaPo"/>
* Director Appleton, [[Science and Engineering Research Council]] (also deputy director, [[Rutherford Appleton Laboratory]])(1979–83)<ref name="archiveis"/>
* Professor of Atmospheric Physics, Oxford University (1973–83).<ref name="archiveis"/>

He was knighted in 1991.<ref name="WaPo">{{cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/local/obituaries/john-houghton-renowned-climate-scientist-who-led-ipcc-reports-dies-of-coronavirus-at-88/2020/04/20/c6b6819c-81ab-11ea-a3ee-13e1ae0a3571_story.html|title=John Houghton, renowned climate scientist who led IPCC reports, dies of coronavirus at 88|newspaper=Washington Post|access-date=21 April 2020}}</ref>  Houghton was an Honorary Scientist of the [[Hadley Centre for Climate Prediction and Research]] at the [[Met Office]] (since 2002); Honorary Scientist at the [[Rutherford Appleton Laboratory]] (since 1991); a Trustee of the [[Shell Foundation]] (since 2000); Chairman of the John Ray Initiative (since 1997)<ref name="japanprize.jp"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.consejoculturalmundial.org/winners/winners-of-the-world-award-of-science/prof-sir-john-houghton/|title=Albert Einstein World Award of Science 2009|date=25 November 2009 |access-date=16 November 2017}}</ref><ref>Bio details heavily drawn from [http://www.st-edmunds.cam.ac.uk/faraday/Advisory.php?UID=17 bio at the] [[Faraday Institute]] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071210053233/http://www.st-edmunds.cam.ac.uk/faraday/Advisory.php?UID=17|date=10 December 2007}}</ref> and in 2013 was announced as an advisory board member for [[Sure Chill (refrigeration technology)|Sure Chill Technology]]. He moved back to Wales and lived in [[Aberdyfi]].<ref>{{cite news|publisher=BBC|title=Scientist's climate change honour|date=16 January 2006|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/wales/north_west/4617056.stm|access-date=2020-04-17}}</ref> In 2007 he criticised the controversial documentary ''[[The Great Global Warming Swindle]]'' for its inaccuracies.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.jri.org.uk/news/Critique_Channel4_Global_Warming_Swindle.pdf |title=Critique Channel4 Global Warming Swindle |access-date=2020-04-17 |archive-date=5 August 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190805200016/http://www.jri.org.uk/news/Critique_Channel4_Global_Warming_Swindle.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref>

He died of complications from [[Alzheimer's disease]] and [[COVID-19]] in hospital at [[Dolgellau]] on 15 April 2020, aged 88.<ref name="BBCobit">{{cite web |title=Welsh climate scientist dies of suspected Covid-19 |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-wales-52325374 |website=BBC News |date=17 April 2020}}</ref><ref name = ODNB/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://weather.com/news/climate/news/2020-04-16-climate-scientist-founding-ipcc-editor-sir-john-houghton-dies|title=Sir John Houghton, Climate Scientist and Founding IPCC Editor, Dies at 88|date=16 April 2020|author=Bob Henson|website=The Weather Channel}}</ref>

* [[Albert Einstein World Award of Science]] (2009)<ref>{{cite web|title=Albert Einstein World Award of Science 2009|date=25 November 2009 |url=http://www.consejoculturalmundial.org/winners/winners-of-the-world-award-of-science/prof-sir-john-houghton/|access-date=16 November 2017}}</ref>
* [[Japan Prize]] (2006)<ref name="WaPo"/>
* [[International Meteorological Organization Prize]] (1998)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://wmo.int/international-meteorological-organization-imo-prize|title=International Meteorological Organization (IMO) Prize|website=World Meteorological Organization|date=9 December 2015 |publisher=World Meteorolical Association (WMO)|access-date=29 May 2018}}</ref>
* [[American Meteorological Society]], Honorary Member (1998)<ref name="RMetS">{{cite web|url=https://www.rmets.org/news/our-thoughts|title=In our thoughts|publisher=Royal Meteorological Society|access-date=21 April 2020}}</ref>
* [[Gold Medal of the Royal Astronomical Society]] (1995)<ref name="WaPo"/>
* [[Global 500 Roll of Honour|Global 500 Award]], under the United Nations Environmental Programme (1994)<ref name="archiveis"/>
* [[Bakerian Lecture]] of the [[Royal Society]] (1991)<ref name="archiveis"/>
* [[Knight Bachelor]] (1991)<ref name="archiveis"/>
* [[Symons Gold Medal]], [[Royal Meteorological Society]] (1990)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rmets.org/sites/default/files/2019-04/awards_history_0.pdf|title=Awards History|publisher=Royal Meteorological Society|access-date=21 April 2020}}</ref>
* [[Richard Glazebrook Medal and Prize]], [[Institute of Physics]], (1990)<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.iop.org/about/awards/gold/glazebrook/medallists/page_38439.html|title=Glazebook Medal Recipients|publisher=IOP|access-date=21 April 2020}}</ref>
* [[William Gaskell Medal]] of the [[Royal Meteorological Society]], (1983)<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.japanprize.jp/en/prize_prof_2006_houghton.html|title= Laureates of the Japan Prize - Sir John Houghton |publisher=Japan Prize Foundation|access-date= 2 April 2017}}</ref>
* [[Institute of Physics Edward Appleton Medal and Prize|The Chree medal and prize]] (1979)<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.iop.org/about/awards/subject/appleton/appleton-medallists/page_38521.html|title=Edward Appleton medal recipients|publisher=IOP|access-date=21 April 2020}}</ref>
* President of the [[Royal Meteorological Society]] (1976–1978)<ref name="RMetS"/>
* Elected [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] (1972)<ref name="WaPo"/><ref>{{Cite journal |last=White |first=Robert S. |date=2022 |title=Sir John Theodore Houghton. 30 December 1931 — 15 April 2020 |journal=Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society |volume=73|pages=291–314 |doi=10.1098/rsbm.2022.0014 |s2cid=250458991 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

He received Honorary Doctorates of Science from the Universities of Wales (1991), Stirling (1992), East Anglia (1993), Leeds (1995), Heriot-Watt (1996), Greenwich (1997), Glamorgan (1998), Reading (1999), Birmingham (2000), Gloucestershire (2001), Hull (2002) and Dalhousie (2010).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Houghton_John|title=Academy of Europe:Houghton John|publisher=Academy of Europe|access-date=21 April 2020}}</ref>  He was an Honorary Fellow of [[Jesus College, Oxford]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.jesus.ox.ac.uk/about-jesus-college/news/2020/april/sir-john-houghton-cbe-frs-flsw|title=Sir John Houghton CBE FRS FLSW|publisher=Jesus College, Oxford|access-date=21 April 2020|archive-date=18 May 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200518193352/https://www.jesus.ox.ac.uk/about-jesus-college/news/2020/april/sir-john-houghton-cbe-frs-flsw|url-status=dead}}</ref> [[University of Wales, Aberystwyth]] and of [[University of Wales, Lampeter]] and was also a Founding Fellow of the [[Learned Society of Wales]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.learnedsociety.wales/founding-fellows/|title=Founding Fellows|publisher=The Learned Society of Wales|access-date=21 April 2020}}</ref>

==Legacy==
A metal sculpture of Sir John Houghton was erected in [[Rhyl]] in 2013, together with figures of two other local celebrities, Don Spendlove and [[Mike Peters (musician)|Mike Peters]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rhyljournal.co.uk/news/15720012.three-icons-of-rhyl-unveiled-at-entrance-to-harbour-bridge/|title=Three icons of Rhyl unveiled at entrance to harbour bridge|website=Rhyl, Prestatyn and Abergele Journal|date=8 October 2013|author=Matt Jones|access-date=17 April 2020}}</ref>

==Misquotation==
In a November 2006 article in Australia's [[The Daily Telegraph (Sydney)|''The Daily Telegraph'']], journalist [[Piers Akerman]] quoted Houghton as saying "Unless we announce disasters, no one will listen", attributing the quotation to his 1994 book ''Global Warming, The Complete Briefing''.  This has since been quoted by many [[global warming scepticism|deniers]], including [[Benny Peiser]] and [[Christopher Monckton, 3rd Viscount Monckton of Brenchley|Christopher Monckton]], and is listed at the top of the front page of [[Christopher Booker]]'s ''[[The Real Global Warming Disaster]]''.  However, the quotation does not appear in any edition of Houghton's book. Houghton never said any such thing and believed the opposite.<ref>{{Citation
 | date = 10 February 2010
 | title = Fabricated quote used to discredit climate scientist
 | periodical = [[The Independent]]
 | url = https://www.independent.co.uk/environment/climate-change/fabricated-quote-used-to-discredit-climate-scientist-1894552.html
 | access-date = 10 February 2010
}}
</ref>
The publishers of ''The Real Global Warming Disaster'', The Continuum International Publishing Group, apologised for the reference to that quotation, confirmed (in addition to Booker's confirmation) that it will not be repeated, and agreed to place a corrigendum in any further copies of the book.

In an article which appeared in ''[[The Sunday Telegraph]]'' on 20 February 2010, Christopher Booker purported to correct the misquotation contained in ''The Real Global Warming Disaster'' but this article contained yet further inaccuracies.<ref>{{Citation
 | date = 20 February 2010
 | title = Article by Christopher Booker in ''The Sunday Telegraph'', "What the weatherman never said"
 | url = https://www.telegraph.co.uk/comment/columnists/christopherbooker/7280369/What-the-weatherman-never-said.html
 | access-date = 10 February 2010
 | work=The Daily Telegraph
}}
</ref> As a result, Houghton referred the matter to the [[Press Complaints Commission]] (PCC Reference 101959). Following the PCC's involvement, ''The Sunday Telegraph'' published on 15 August 2010 a letter of correction by Houghton stating his true position.<ref>{{Citation
 | date = 15 August 2010
 | title = Letter by Sir John Houghton in The Sunday Telegraph, 15 August 2010
 | url = https://www.telegraph.co.uk/comment/letters/7944874/Trident-shouldnt-lead-to-more-defence-cuts.html
 | access-date = 9 January 2010
 | work=The Sunday Telegraph
}}
</ref> An article supportive of Houghton also appeared in the edition of 21 May 2010 of ''New Scientist''.<ref>{{Citation
 | date = May 2010

 | title = "Living in denial: Unleashing a lie", Jim Giles, ''New Scientist'', 21 May 2010
 | url = https://www.newscientist.com/article/mg20627606.300-living-in-denial-unleashing-a-lie.html
 | access-date = 9 January 2010
 | work=New Scientist
}}
</ref>

The correct quotation was, "If we want a good environmental policy in the future we'll have to have a disaster. It's like safety on public transport. The only way humans will act is if there's been an accident."<ref>{{Citation
 | date = 10 August 1995

 | title = 'Me and My God', Sir John Houghton talks to Frances Welch, 10 August 1995
 | url =  http://john-adams.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2010/02/houghton-and-god.pdf
}}
</ref>
